narrative.what_i_did:
Opened with the operator's directive 'Fire up and tackle next batch.' Read the prior session's full hand-off honest, confirmed the repo lock (stackingunderpressure/tapit-wallet matches), and ran the four gates clean before touching anything — typecheck silent, lint silent, 258 of 258 tests in 8.49 seconds, build clean. Treated the operator's 'next batch' as authorization for the prior carpenter's recommended next-session option (a): cut the peer-side vouch-witness surface so the vouch loop closes end-to-end on the other half the prior session left open. The prior session shipped the joiner-side loop-back routing fix and the JoinOrgModal live-self-membership progress chip; the gap that remained was that when a vouching peer first receives the joiner's 1-sig self-membership envelope to sign on, routeFor classified it as self-membership-receive (because the receiver was not the envelope subject) and HomeScreen.routeInbox dispatched to acceptSelfMembership which warns-and-returns silently on the peer's non-org wallet — the peer saw no surface to vouch with, which meant the joiner could fan their envelope out but no peer could actually do anything with it on the receiving end.

The substantive shape of the cut is a three-position receiver discriminator inside the isSelfMembership branch of routeFor. Position one (joiner loop-back, receiver IS subject, more than one signature) was the prior session's fix and routes to absorb-cosign. Position two (peer-side vouch arrival, receiver is NEITHER subject NOR the org named in the org_id leaf, exactly one signature) is the new branch this cut added and routes to a fresh vouch-witness InboxRouteAction with label 'Vouch' and the hint 'A peer is asking you to vouch for their join request.' Position three (org-side accept, receiver IS the org named in org_id, any signature count) falls through to self-membership-receive and runs the org's declared join-policy gate. envelopeRoute.test.ts grew from 8 to 10 dispatch tests covering the new peer-side route and explicitly locking the position-three discriminator so a future routing refactor cannot accidentally steal direct-submission joins from the org by overgeneralizing the vouch-witness branch. The new branch imports leafValue from createHandshake to read the org_id off the envelope; comparisons are case-insensitive via toLowerCase on both sides, matching the convention every other pubkey-comparison helper in the codebase uses.

The peer-facing modal is VouchWitnessModal in src/features/cosigning/, lazy-loaded from HomeScreen via the same React.lazy + Suspense pattern the other inbox-routed modals use. It opens pre-loaded with the joiner's envelope, reads the self-membership view via readSelfMembership, resolves the joiner's display name via peerNamesByPubkey from the peer's own holdings (falling back to a short pubkey rendering when the peer has no handshake with the joiner), and shows a review step framed as personal trust rather than co-authorship — 'Sam is asking you to vouch for their join request to Acme. Vouching means attaching your signature as a personal warrant.' On confirm, the modal calls wallet.sign on the existing envelope (the keys-never-leave rule preserved — only the public envelope crosses the wire), advances to a signed step with a Send-vouch-back button, and dispatches the signed envelope via sendEnvelope to view.joinerId (NOT to incomingSender, because a hypothetical relay-peer who forwarded the envelope is not the absorb-target; the joiner is the one whose AbsorbCosignModal needs to merge the vouch). Status text from summarizePublish renders next to the button, copy + QR + Share fallbacks ride alongside for the no-Mycelium path. The modal mounts in HomeScreen the same way RecoveryResponderModal does — incomingForVouch + incomingEventIdForVouch state, a vouch-witness branch in routeInbox, and a Suspense-wrapped mount that dismisses the matching inbox row on success.

The size doctrine forced an extraction in the same commit. HomeScreen was at 797 lines before the cut, three under the 800-line hard limit, and the vouch-witness surface needed roughly fifteen new lines of state plus modal mount which would have pushed the file over. The clean move was to extract the three async accept-helpers (acceptRecoveryShare, acceptMembership, acceptSelfMembership) into a new useInboxAccepts hook in src/features/wallet-core/ — they share a homogeneous shape (verify-via-feature-module, hold-and-anchor, save, refresh, dismiss matching inbox row) so they cluster naturally into one place. The hook takes orgDeclaration as its only parameter (because that lookup is computed in HomeScreen via findOwnOrgDeclaration over holdings) and internally pulls wallet/ownerId/anchorWorker/identity/holdings/inboxEnvelopes/dismissInboxEnvelope/save/refresh from useWallet. The HomeScreen useWallet destructure shrank correspondingly (ownerId, anchorWorker, save, refresh dropped — no longer referenced at HomeScreen scope post-extraction), and the inline acceptRecoveryShare + acceptMembership + acceptSelfMembership function declarations were replaced by a single destructuring of the hook's return value placed right after the orgDeclaration useMemo. Net effect: HomeScreen went from 797 to 766 lines (31 lines of headroom restored), and the inbox-acceptance logic now lives in one place where future inbox-route accept-helpers (e.g. roster-update-accept, charter-amendment-accept in Phase D) can land without re-growing HomeScreen.

Four gates all green after: typecheck silent, lint silent, 260 of 260 tests passing in 8.30 seconds (no flake on this run, including the transport.test.ts chat-versus-envelope subscription isolation assertion the prior session flagged), build clean with no bundle-budget overages from the new VouchWitnessModal lazy chunk (it ships in the cosigning helpers chunk per the existing vite manualChunks config). HomeScreen.tsx settled at 766 lines, envelopeRoute.ts at 138 lines, envelopeRoute.test.ts at 186 lines, useInboxAccepts.ts at 121 lines new, VouchWitnessModal.tsx at 294 lines new. The cosigning and wallet-core manifests both picked up paragraphs naming the vouch-witness surface and the useInboxAccepts extraction; the transport manifest's prior-session paragraph about the peer-side gap got rewritten to name this cut as the gap closure.
narrative.whats_pending:
The vouch loop now closes end-to-end at the substrate level. The joiner-side CosignRequestModal in org_vouch mode fans the 1-sig envelope out to N peers via Mycelium (prior session); each of those peers' wallets routes the arrival to vouch-witness and surfaces VouchWitnessModal pre-loaded with the envelope (this session); each peer signs and sends back through encryptedInbox to the joiner (this session); the joiner's wallet routes the returned cosigned envelope to absorb-cosign via the loop-back receiver discriminator (prior session); AbsorbCosignModal merges the vouch into the held copy and the JoinOrgModal progress chip ticks up by one (prior session). The remaining work on this loop is field-testing on real devices — the operator should be able to walk through a full vouch flow with two physical wallets and see the joiner-side progress chip tick from 0 to 1 to 2 as peer wallets respond.

The next natural Phase E4 cuts are now the other follow-ups the prior session named. The Phase D charter-amendment chain (multi-session, brief lands in project-memory/foreman-memory/projects/tapit-wallet/briefs/charter-amendment-chain-roadmap.md) is the largest thread — it will probably need the same receiver-aware routing pattern this loop's substrate uses, because an amendment envelope can legitimately flow through proposer, voter, and ratifier positions with different correct actions at each. The receiveSelfMembership orgSelfDecl-lookup centralization is a smaller one-session cut that moves the org-declaration discovery out of HomeScreen and into the receive function itself, reducing the orgDeclaration parameter useInboxAccepts has to take. The appcommander metadata cleanup chip is still on the menu pending operator confirmation of whether the AppCommander cockpit polls those files from origin/main.

The JoinOrgModal file is at 670 lines — well under the 800-line hard limit but over the 400 soft warn (unchanged this session because this cut did not touch JoinOrgModal). The natural extraction candidate when JoinOrgModal next needs touching remains the two proof-candidate finders findHandshakeProofCandidates and findCredentialProofCandidates plus their pure-logic helpers (describeHandshakePeer, isCredentialAttestation, isRelationshipAttestation); they could move cleanly to src/features/connections/joinOrgProofCandidates.ts as a sibling module and would carry a clear unit-test surface (which the inline JoinOrgModal code currently has none of). That would buy back roughly 50 lines.

A small UX consideration worth surfacing for a future cut: VouchWitnessModal does not currently surface any indication of whether the peer holds a handshake with the joiner before they decide to vouch. The display-name fallback to short-pubkey is the signal (if the joiner shows as a hex string, the peer has no handshake with them), but that is an indirect tell and the operator might miss it. A future polish cut could add an explicit warning banner in the review step when peerNames lacks the joiner's pubkey — something like 'You do not have a handshake with this person yet. Vouching means warranting their identity to the organization, so make sure you know who you are signing for.' Not adding it now because the cut is already chunk-shaped and the implicit signal is honest, but naming the seam so the next carpenter can see the polish opportunity.
narrative.what_you_could_do_better:
Two honest observations. First, the useInboxAccepts hook takes orgDeclaration as a parameter rather than computing it internally, because the orgDeclaration lookup is a useMemo in HomeScreen that depends on holdings + wallet.identity and HomeScreen already uses it in multiple other useMemos (issuedMemberships, officialsRoster, the JSX render conditions). Recomputing it inside the hook would duplicate work and create two sources of truth that could in principle diverge under React's render scheduling. The honest answer is probably that the orgDeclaration lookup itself should move into useWallet (it is wallet-level state, not screen-level state) and then both HomeScreen and useInboxAccepts could pull it from useWallet directly. That is a larger refactor that crosses into the receiveSelfMembership orgSelfDecl-lookup centralization thread the prior session named — naming the seam in this narrative so a future carpenter can see that the two refactors are actually the same refactor seen from different angles.

Second observation: VouchWitnessModal duplicates the canonicalEnvelope-display + copy + QR + share + sendBack scaffolding that CosignAsWitnessModal already has on its signed step, with only minor framing differences in the button labels and the destination address (view.joinerId vs incomingSender). The honest read is that there is a generic 'signed-envelope-return surface' primitive trying to surface — paste-step optional, review-step framing variable per kind, signed-step shared. Pulling that out would be the right move when a third caller appears with the same shape (probably the Phase D charter-amendment voter surface). I deliberately did not attempt the extraction in this cut because it would have doubled the chunk size and the shared-primitive shape is still speculative — two callers do not yet justify the abstraction, especially when the framing differences (vouch language vs cosign language) are exactly the kind of thing that would push back against a too-rigid shared component. The pattern note worth lifting into doctrine is probably 'three callers minimum before extracting a shared modal primitive,' which fits the operator's broader 'composition over invention' framing.
narrative.bigger_picture:
Loop closure is the bigger-picture teaching of this cut and the prior cut together. The CosignRequestModal fan-out, the peer-side vouch-witness signing surface, the send-back via Mycelium, the joiner-side loop-back routing, the AbsorbCosignModal merge, and the JoinOrgModal progress chip are six pieces that together make up one composite primitive: collaborative attestation collection across N parties on a single envelope. Any one piece in isolation is partial. The joiner-side fan-out without a peer-side response surface is a button that does nothing. A peer-side response surface without joiner-side absorb routing is a vouch that never reaches the joiner. An absorb routing without UI feedback is a merge the operator cannot see. The work the operator authorized as 'next batch' was the second-to-last piece in a six-piece composite that took three sessions to land — and now that the composite is whole, the next person who uses the wallet to vouch for a peer's join request sees a coherent experience rather than a half-built mechanism.

The deeper substrate pattern this two-session arc surfaces is what 'composition over invention' actually looks like at the modal layer. The new VouchWitnessModal is structurally a sibling of CosignAsWitnessModal — they share roughly 80% of their state, their signed-step UI, and their send-back-via-Mycelium scaffolding — but the framing they put around the signing decision is meaningfully different (personal-trust vs co-authorship) and that framing IS the product. The operator's experience of being asked 'do you vouch for this person joining this org' is not the same as being asked 'do you co-sign this fact about your relationship,' and conflating the two would erode trust in both. The right architectural answer is therefore not to fold VouchWitnessModal into CosignAsWitnessModal with a 'mode' prop (which is what a too-rigid composition reflex would do), but to keep them as siblings sharing a substrate (wallet.sign, sendEnvelope, summarizePublish, EnvelopePreview, the canonicalEnvelope display pattern) while presenting distinct surfaces. The Layer 2 to Layer 4 ladder lives at the substrate; the Layer 4 framing is what makes each surface feel like the right thing to do in that moment.

The receiver-aware routing primitive that handles three positions in one branch (joiner-loop-back, peer-arrival, org-receipt) is the routing-layer analogue of the same pattern. routeFor could in principle have been fragmented into routeForJoinerLoopBack, routeForVouchingPeer, and routeForOrg — but doing so would have meant the InboxPanel + ScanEnvelopeModal + future-transport callers each having to know which routing function to call based on context they should not need to know. Instead the single routeFor primitive absorbs the variation by taking a small amount of receiver context, dispatching internally based on the envelope shape AND the receiver position. The pattern extends cleanly to future multi-position envelope kinds (the charter-amendment chain the operator has on the roadmap will probably have similar four-or-five position semantics), and the cost of extension is one new branch inside the isSelfMembership block plus one new InboxRouteAction value rather than a new top-level routing primitive. That ratio of composition to invention is what makes the layer-climbing feel manageable rather than overwhelming, and it is the pattern this two-session arc has now demonstrated three times in slightly different shapes — the discriminated-union for CosignRequestModal's orgContext prop (prior arc), the receiver-aware routing for routeFor (this session and last), and the hook-extraction for useInboxAccepts (this session). The shape rhymes.

feedback_to_appcommander: Three patterns from this two-session arc worth lifting into the AppCommander-side doctrine. First, the receiver-aware-routing pattern this session and last together demonstrated: routing primitives that dispatch from envelope shape alone work for kinds where shape is unambiguous, but kinds whose envelopes can legitimately arrive at multiple network positions with different correct actions need receiver context passed through. The fix pattern is to add an optional receiver parameter with back-compat fall-through, do the disambiguation only inside the kind branch that needs it, and update callers incrementally. The vouch loop substrate now has three receiver positions in one isSelfMembership branch (joiner-loop-back, peer-arrival, org-receipt) which proves the pattern scales past two positions cleanly. Future multi-position envelope kinds (the charter-amendment chain on the roadmap) will extend this pattern further. Second, the 'composition over invention at the modal layer' pattern: CosignAsWitnessModal and VouchWitnessModal share 80% of their substrate but present distinct surfaces because the framing IS the product. The right architectural answer is to keep them as siblings sharing primitives (wallet.sign, sendEnvelope, summarizePublish, EnvelopePreview) rather than folding them into one modal with a 'mode' prop. Probably worth a doctrine note about the three-callers-minimum threshold before extracting a shared modal primitive. Third, the inbox-acceptance-helper extraction pattern: the three async accept-helpers in HomeScreen (acceptRecoveryShare, acceptMembership, acceptSelfMembership) shared a homogeneous shape and clustered naturally into useInboxAccepts when HomeScreen needed size headroom for a new inbox-routing surface. The hook takes the only screen-scoped dependency (orgDeclaration) as a parameter and pulls everything else from useWallet. This is the wallet-core layer's recipe for absorbing horizontal complexity without overflowing the orchestrator file; future skeletons with a similar inbox-routing pattern can pre-seed the hook scaffolding. Open question for AppCommander operator stays the same as prior sessions: confirm whether the cockpit polls appcommander/DOCTRINE_MANIFEST.json and appcommander/cockpit-cards.json from origin/main externally — if not, the entire appcommander/ folder can be removed in a follow-up cut and the skeleton bundle no longer needs to seed it.
